title: Elevator Cab Weight Failure
summary: This note details an instance where a design decision at Otis Elevator Company led to an elevator cab exceeding its maximum weight limit due to failing to follow standard operating procedures. The owner acknowledged the mistake, worked with engineering and the client to redesign the cab, and implemented a pre-fabrication checklist to prevent a repeat.

key_points.text: Received critical feedback after a design decision did not follow standard operating procedures
Requested premium customizations, including heavy wood wall panels and Italian marble flooring inside the elevator cab
Made a judgment call without completing the full SOP verification and approved the design for fabrication without formally verifying the final cab weight
Elevator cab was over the maximum weight limit, which meant that it would fail final state inspections
Worked with engineering and the client to redesign the cab, ultimately replacing the marble flooring with thin-set tiles to bring the cab back within weight limits
Redesign caused project delays and resulted in financial losses for Otis
Created a pre-fabrication checklist that highlighted the most common pitfalls, shared it with other project managers
Since implementing this checklist, there has not been a repeat issue, and it has been adopted informally by peers as a final quality check before fabrication release

differences: The excerpts use slightly different phrasing for the same events, such as describing the action of releasing the elevator into fabrication without verifying weight.
